newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurds to begin second round of peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds to begin second round of peace talks.

text.p: Two rival Kurdish factions on Friday begin a second round of U.S.-brokered talks in Ankara to consolidate a three-week-old ceasefire in northern Iraq, the Turkish foreign ministry said.
U.S. diplomat Robert Pelletreau arrived in Turkey late on Thursday to attend the meeting.

Pelletreau presided over the first round of peace talks in October between Massoud Barzani's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Jalal Talabani's Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), where the feuding groups agreed to extend a U.S.-brokered ceasefire that took hold after nearly two months of fighting.

Pelletreau, who is overseeing the talks along with British and Turkish diplomats, said on his arrival that the second round of talks would focus on providing humanitarian aid to northern Iraq and restoring services in the region.

The two factions began fighting after Iraqi armoured divisions joined forces with Barzani's KDP in late August to capture the regional capital Arbil from the PUK, prompting U.S missile strikes against targets in southern Iraq.
The status of Arbil and the sharing of KDP oil trade revenues on the Turkish border are the key issues which need to be resolved in the longer term, mediators said.
Disputes over those two key issues effectively killed a Kurdish attempt at parliamentary self-rule in northern Iraq after Western-sponsored elections in the region in 1992.
